newsitem.title: USA: Patina Oil says 1996 reserves increase.
newsitem.headline: Patina Oil says 1996 reserves increase.

text.p: Patina Oil & Gas Corp said on Monday its proved reserves totaled 71.9 million barrels of oil equivalents at year-end 1996.
Reserve quantities rose 135 percent above the level reported one year earlier, primarily from the acquisition of Gerrity Oil and Gas in May 1996, the company said.

The pretax present value of the reserves, based on constant prices and costs and discounted at 10 percent, reached $649 million, a more than four-fold increase from the year-end 1995 level, the company said.
Patina said the sharp increase in reserve value during 1996 was caused by a combination of the Gerrity acquisition and substantial increases in oil and gas prices during the year.
Patina said it expects to be profitable for 1996, as well as the fourth quarter, when it reports its results in 30 days.

During 1996, Patina produced 1.7 million barrels of oil and 23.9 billion cubic feet of natural gas or a total of 5.7 million barrels of oil equivalent, indicating a year-end reserve life index of 12.7 years.
At year-end, production averaged 5,100 barrels of oil and 72.5 million cubic feet per day of natural gas, Patina said.
In 1996, the Company drilled 21 development wells and recompleted a further 61 wells at a total cost of approximately $8 million.

A preliminary capital budget of $14 million has been established for 1997 for the drilling of 35 wells and 75 recompletions as well as other plans to boost production from its existing wells, Patina said.
